A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Skip-DiT research. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the main paper and supplement.

before.justification: v4 reports original Skip-DiT training and inference experiments, image/video generation benchmarks, ablations and qualitative examples in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experimental results, including the block-selection and few-step experiments moved into the supplement.

M1.justification: The skip-connection fusion in Equation 4, two-stage continual training and cached inference procedure in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Shortened backbone descriptions do not establish an architectural or procedural revision.

E1.justification: The ImageNet, MS-COCO, class-to-video datasets, Vimeo training data and VBench evaluation coverage are retained. Shortening Webvid-10M and Vimeo-2M to Webvid and Vimeo does not indicate different data being used.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. This includes AdaCache and TeaCache in Table 2, Faster-Diff in Appendix Table 10, and the caching-method compatibility comparisons in Table 6.

E3.justification: Sampling schedules, cache settings, sample counts, training budgets and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Although Table 4 loses its guidance-scale and checkpoint details, cfg=1.5 remains documented in Table 10 and the 2.9M-step checkpoint in Section 4.3.

E4.justification: The perturbation, caching-phase, compatibility, block-selection, few-step and scheduler analyses are retained, together with the qualitative case studies. Tables 7–8 and their discussions move from Section 4.4 to supplementary Section 7 without new analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 3 reports means and standard deviations across samples in both versions. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added or changed.

E6.justification: The numerical table entries and graphical results match, including relocated Tables 7–8. For example, Table 2 retains Skip-DiT's uncached VBench score of 75.60, and Table 9 retains FID 8.37 at 2.9M training steps. The qualitative images also match.

T1.justification: The assumptions, two theorems, equations and detailed proofs are unchanged. The Lipschitz comparison shortened from the main-text discussion remains elsewhere, including the supplement; the proof section is renumbered from 7 to 8.

C1.justification: The central feature-stability and training/inference acceleration claims remain. However, v5's shorter conclusion drops the explicit claim of seamless integration enabling real-time image and video generation, modestly narrowing its concluding assertions.

C2.justification: The explanations of feature stability, caching phases and metric fluctuations are retained. Section 6's computational, data, parameter-overhead and memory limitations move intact into the supplement rather than being removed or revised.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 omits the 10M and 2M qualifiers from the training-source names, slightly reducing identification specificity. Sample counts, preprocessing, hardware, training durations, caching configurations and code-access information otherwise remain documented.

R1.justification: The same 54 references remain. The condensed LSC discussion drops the explicit assertion that statistic-cached inference is absent from other models and the claim that U-DiT doubles feature dimensions, while retaining the principal architectural and pretrained-model compatibility contrasts.

P1.justification: v5 condenses the contributions, related work, model descriptions and conclusion, removes the general DiT architecture primer, and updates an author affiliation. Limitations and two existing analyses move into the supplement; the main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: All 13 tables and 9 figures are retained. Tables 7–8 move into the supplement, several captions are shortened, and figures and tables are repositioned as surrounding text reflows. The underlying graphics and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 primarily condenses and reorganizes v4 while preserving its method, proofs and complete experimental evidence. Shorter prose and a more restrained conclusion offer modest benefits, while abbreviated dataset names and captions reduce some immediate specificity. These limited editorial tradeoffs do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
